instructions.summary: The subscription covers 25 named users for internal business work. You can replace users without adding seats. The customer owns their data; we own the software.
instructions.howToExplainToBuyers: Your data stays yours. We only process it to run and secure the service, provide support, or meet legal duties—not to sell it or train general-purpose AI.
instructions.commonObjections: Customers may worry staff changes mean buying extra seats, or want to share logins or give others access.
instructions.negotiation: Explain that replacing a user needs no extra seat. For more users, agree a written order. Different access rights or pricing need Legal and Finance.

instructions.summary: The software must work substantially as its documentation describes. If we cannot fix a serious mismatch within 30 days of written notice, the customer can end the affected subscription.
instructions.howToExplainToBuyers: We aim to reply within one business day during 9–5 Pacific support hours; that is not a fix deadline. Cancellation under this warranty refunds unused prepaid fees and cancels remaining fees for that period.
instructions.commonObjections: Customers commonly want weekend support, guaranteed fix times, or a refund if the software does not work as described.
instructions.negotiation: Explain the existing fix-or-refund protection. If they need guaranteed response or repair times or extra support hours, ask Legal and Finance before committing.

instructions.summary: We invoice $24,000 USD at the start of each subscription year, plus applicable sales tax. Payment is due 30 days after receipt.
instructions.howToExplainToBuyers: We can give you 45 days to pay without approval. That changes the deadline, not the annual invoice or year-long commitment.
instructions.commonObjections: Customers commonly request more time to pay or smaller, more frequent invoices. These are different changes.
instructions.negotiation: Offer 45 days for payment-processing delays. If the annual bill is the problem, request Finance approval for quarterly invoices at net 30. Choose one option.

concessions.description: Give the customer 45 days after invoice receipt to pay, without approval. Keep annual billing and change the deadline in both the agreement and Order Form.
With Finance approval, split the annual fee into four quarterly invoices, initially $6,000 USD each before tax. Keep net 30 and update both invoice schedules.

replacement.text: Provider will invoice the annual subscription fee in four equal quarterly installments, each equal to one-quarter of that subscription year’s annual fee, at the beginning of each three-month period of that subscription year.

Four equal quarterly installments at the beginning of each three-month period of each subscription year, each equal to one-quarter of that year’s annual fee; $6,000 USD per installment in the initial year; first invoice January 1, 2027

instructions.summary: Customers can dispute an invoice within 30 days and must pay the part they agree with. Overdue, undisputed amounts can attract interest and suspension after written warning.
instructions.howToExplainToBuyers: A reasonable billing dispute does not trigger late charges or suspension over that amount. Suspension requires 15 days’ written warning and preserves data-export rights.
instructions.commonObjections: Customers may worry a billing mistake will cut off access. Others object to late charges or need more time to pay.
instructions.negotiation: Point out the disputed-bill protection and warning period. Offer preapproved net 45 for payment delays; changing late charges or suspension rights needs Legal and Finance.

instructions.summary: The subscription runs for 2027, then renews in one-year terms unless either side gives written notice at least 30 days before the current term ends.
instructions.howToExplainToBuyers: You can stop the next renewal without an extra charge by emailing the notice address on time. Changing plans does not let you cancel the current year.
instructions.commonObjections: Customers may want to avoid automatic renewal or cancel at any time. Stopping the next term and ending the current one have different consequences.
instructions.negotiation: Show them the nonrenewal deadline and notice email. Early cancellation or changes to renewal terms need Legal and Finance; explain the current year remains committed.

instructions.summary: Prices can increase by up to 5% at renewal, with 60 days’ written notice. Without timely notice, the current fee applies for the next year.
instructions.howToExplainToBuyers: We must tell you about an increase before your nonrenewal deadline, giving you time to decide. Your current-year price does not change.
instructions.commonObjections: Customers commonly ask for a smaller increase or a price that cannot change without their agreement.
instructions.negotiation: Offer the preapproved 3% limit. If they need control over every increase, request Finance approval to keep the current fee unless both sides agree otherwise in writing.

concessions.description: Lower the maximum renewal increase from 5% to 3%, without approval. The 60-day written notice still applies.
With Finance approval, keep the current renewal fee unless both sides agree a different price in writing.

replacement.text: The existing annual subscription fee applies for each renewal term unless both parties agree a different fee in writing. Provider has no unilateral right to increase the renewal fee. Other commercial changes require both parties’ written agreement.

instructions.summary: Either side can end the agreement for a serious breach left unfixed for 30 days after written notice, or if the other stops operating or has insolvency proceedings open for 60 days.
instructions.howToExplainToBuyers: If you end it for our uncorrected breach or insolvency, we refund unused prepaid fees within 30 days and cancel remaining fees for that period.
instructions.commonObjections: Customers may want immediate cancellation or refunds when they are at fault. If we end it for their breach, committed current-term fees remain due.
instructions.negotiation: Use their example to explain the 30-day fix period and who owes what. Shorter deadlines, broader cancellation rights, or different refunds need Legal and Finance.

instructions.summary: Both sides protect private information for three years after the agreement ends. Trade secrets stay protected while secret; customer data stays protected while retained.
instructions.howToExplainToBuyers: Only people who need the information for this agreement can see it, including contractors bound to keep it confidential. We remain responsible for our contractors.
instructions.commonObjections: Customers may want protection forever or a separate confidentiality agreement. Trade secrets and retained customer data already have longer protection.
instructions.negotiation: Point out the longer protection for trade secrets and retained data. A different duration or separate confidentiality agreement needs Legal.

instructions.summary: We protect customer data and report confirmed unauthorized access or disclosure within 72 hours. Free exports remain available for 30 days after the agreement ends.
instructions.howToExplainToBuyers: The incident deadline starts when we confirm the breach, without waiting for a completed investigation. Active data is deleted within 60 days; backups within 90, unless law requires retention.
instructions.commonObjections: Customers may need specific certifications, storage locations, or safeguards for sensitive data. The agreement does not promise those.
instructions.negotiation: Explain the existing safeguards and free export. Specific security or storage commitments need Legal and Finance. Agree required data-processing terms before processing; do not promise sensitive-data support.

instructions.summary: Each side has one total limit across claims: six months of subscription fees, initially $12,000 USD from day one. Lost profits and indirect losses are generally excluded.
instructions.howToExplainToBuyers: Security, confidentiality, and covered copyright or patent claims share each side’s limit. Due fees and promised refunds are not capped; neither are fraud, deliberate misconduct, or liability the law forbids limiting.
instructions.commonObjections: Customers commonly say the cap is too low or want security and confidentiality claims outside it. The cap is not a fresh allowance per claim.
instructions.negotiation: Explain that the cap applies even before fees are paid. If they need more cover, propose twelve months of fees, subject to Legal approval.

concessions.description: With Legal approval, raise each side’s total cap to twelve months of fees, initially $24,000 USD. The other calculation rules and exceptions stay the same.

replacement.text: Each party’s total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement, across all claims, is limited to twelve months of subscription fees. For this calculation, one month equals one-twelfth of the annual subscription fee payable for the subscription year in which the earliest event giving rise to any claim against that party occurred. The cap therefore equals the full annual fee, regardless of invoice timing or fees paid so far. It excludes taxes and is not reduced by service refunds or credits. For an event after the subscription ends, use the final subscription year’s annual fee. At the initial $24,000 annual fee, the cap is $24,000, including on the first day of the term.

instructions.summary: We defend covered copyright or patent claims against permitted use of our software and pay covered court awards or approved settlements, within the liability cap.
instructions.howToExplainToBuyers: Tell us promptly about a claim. We handle the defense, but need your written consent to admit your fault or make you do anything beyond paying money.
instructions.commonObjections: Customers may want coverage for their uploaded content or a higher cap. Claims caused by their content, unauthorized changes, or certain combinations are excluded.
instructions.negotiation: Explain that our software is already covered. A higher general cap needs Legal; broader claim coverage or changes to defense and payment duties need Legal and Finance.

instructions.summary: We can list the customer’s name and logo on our website, following their brand guidelines. This does not permit testimonials, case studies, press releases, or implied endorsement.
instructions.howToExplainToBuyers: This only lets us list you as a customer. Withdraw permission in writing and we remove the listing within ten business days; the same deadline applies when the agreement ends.
instructions.commonObjections: Customers may require marketing approval before any public use, or prefer not to be listed at all.
instructions.negotiation: Offer the preapproved change requiring written permission before name or logo use. They can decline permission. Broader marketing rights need Legal.

concessions.description: Require the customer’s written permission before public name or logo use. Applying this change needs no internal approval; the customer can decline permission.

replacement.text: Provider must obtain Customer’s prior written consent before using Customer’s name or logo publicly. This Agreement grants no standing publicity permission. Any permitted use must comply with the scope of that written consent and any brand guidelines Customer supplies, and must not imply an endorsement unless expressly authorized in that consent.

instructions.summary: Either side can transfer the agreement in a merger or sale of almost all relevant business assets without consent, if the new company accepts all obligations in writing.
instructions.howToExplainToBuyers: The transferring company must give prompt written notice. Other transfers need consent, which neither side can unreasonably refuse, delay, or attach conditions to.
instructions.commonObjections: Customers may worry this blocks an acquisition or want transfers to related companies. A transfer to a related company is not automatically covered.
instructions.negotiation: Explain that mergers and sales of almost all relevant business assets already have an exception, with written acceptance and prompt notice. Broader transfer rights need Legal.

instructions.summary: California law applies and disputes go to San Francisco courts. The Order Form sets commercial details; other overrides must identify the changed section and be signed by both sides.
instructions.howToExplainToBuyers: Purchase-order terms do not change this agreement. If an outside event prevents material service delivery for over 30 days, you can end it with unused fees refunded or canceled.
instructions.commonObjections: Customers may want their own courts or purchase-order terms. Neither applies automatically just because it appears in their paperwork.
instructions.negotiation: Show where the agreed terms and notice emails belong. Different courts or contract wording need Legal and Finance; a purchase order alone cannot override the agreement.
